newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt bounces with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt bounces with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Prices of emerging market bonds recovered from the slide of the past two days as the U.S. Treasuries moved higher.
Yield spreads of Brady bonds over Treasuries narrowed today, but over the week the changes were negligible, market sources said.

"Dealers marked prices down and then marked them up," said a Brady trader, noting that outside money had practically dried up this week and all the bullish talks about the coming year could not mask the nervousness in the market.
Argentina FRB rose one full point to 85-1/8 bid and Brazil C gained 7/8 to 72.00 bid.
Demand for longer-dated papers pushed Mexico UMS-26 up 1-1/2 points to bid 103-5/8, a market source said.

The market is at the "inflection point" to assess when the Federal Reserve would raise interest rate, said Walter Molano, Latin America economist at SBC/Warburg. "There's going to be a lot of volatility in the first quarter (of 1997),"
Recent remarks by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan was interpreted by some market participants that a tightening would come sooner rather than later, he said.
A rate hike in next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, however, is still seen as unlikely, Molano said.
Bulgaria Bradies languished at lower levels after being buoyed briefly by short-covering, traders said.
Bulgaria FLRB was off 1/8 at 37-1/2 bid.

The political wrangling over Russia's 1997 draft budget in the parliament and how the International Monetary Fund might disburse the withheld loans weighed on Minfin bonds, a trader said. Min Fin 3 and Min Fin 5 added 1/8 to bid 83-1/2 and 41-3/4 respectively, but other Min Fin bonds were off by 3/8.
Vnesh loans and when-issued principal firmed as the perceived "deal risk" diminished, he said, referring to restructuring agreement on those loans to be inked in 1997.
Dollar Vnesh rose one point to bid 76-5/8 and Russia W/I Principal climbed 1-1/8 to 56-1/4.
